business_problem: BT Group wanted to modernize product development by reducing tedious, repetitive, and time-consuming coding work for software engineers while keeping transparency, accountability, intellectual property compliance, and data privacy under responsible controls.
solution_summary: BT Group’s Digital Unit deployed Amazon CodeWhisperer from AWS as a generative AI coding companion embedded in the integrated development environments used by its software engineers. In this implementation, engineers provide the working context through natural-language comments and existing code, and Amazon CodeWhisperer generates real-time suggestions ranging from short snippets to full functions across multiple programming languages. BT also uses the service’s security capabilities to flag hard-to-detect vulnerabilities and propose remediation code inside the development workflow. The rollout was governed by BT Group’s responsible tech guardrails for transparency, accountability, intellectual property compliance, and data privacy, and was supported by onboarding sessions plus a Digital Campus learning pathway. The source does not describe a separate storage tier; the service is delivered directly into developer tooling for engineers to accept or reject suggestions during coding.

solution_components.name: Amazon CodeWhisperer
solution_components.role: Provides real-time generative AI coding assistance, vulnerability scanning, and remediation suggestions inside BT engineers' development workflow.

data_flow: Engineers write natural-language comments and existing code in their IDEs, and Amazon CodeWhisperer uses that context to generate real-time code suggestions, from snippets to full functions, back into the IDE. The same workflow can flag hard-to-detect vulnerabilities and suggest remediations, after which engineers accept or reject the generated output in their normal development process.

business_outcome: BT Group improved software engineering productivity, reduced repetitive coding effort, and enabled faster delivery while introducing responsible AI guardrails and controls around training-data transparency, intellectual property, and privacy.
